zh: 有了 Stripe Treasury，你的业务接受付款的地方，也是你可以存储余额、转移资金并向全球供应商付款的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're building for global scale, get a business bank account that lets your money move instantly.
zh: 如果你正在为全球化规模而构建，找一个能让你的资金即时流动的商业银行账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: whenever and wherever you need it.
zh: 在你需要的任何时候、任何地方。

zh: 在 stripe.com 斜杠 treasury 了解更多。

zh: 当你通过你的业务积累了可观的财富时，它往往被锁定在单一的股票头寸中。

speaker: Unknown
en: The upside is real, but so is the risk, and knowing when to act isn't always obvious.
zh: 上行空间是真实的，但风险也是真实的，而知道何时行动并不总是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creative Planning works with business owners to build a strategy around concentrated equity, when to diversify, how to manage tax risk, and how to protect what you've spent years building.
zh: Creative Planning 与企业主合作，围绕集中持股制定策略，何时多元化，如何管理税务风险，以及如何保护你多年打造的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creative Planning, where wealth works together.
zh: Creative Planning，让财富协同运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at creativeplanning.com slash masters of scale.
zh: 在 creativeplanning.com 斜杠 masters of scale 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine being on your board or an investor in your company and asking the question, what happens if Airbnb wakes up tomorrow and says they're going to do the same thing?
zh: 我想象自己是你们董事会成员或你公司的投资者，问一个问题：如果 Airbnb 明天醒来说他们要做同样的事情，会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, every time we raise money, that is a big question.
zh: 是的，每次我们融资，这都是一个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I have said to that in the past is that when you want to get outside, that's such a different mindset than when you're looking for, you know, a good alternative to a hotel or a house to rent.
zh: 我过去对此的回答是，当你想出去户外时，那与你寻找一家酒店的好的替代方案或一处出租房屋时的心态完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a different use case and a different brand.
zh: 这只是不同的使用场景和不同的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think while there's some overlap in customers, it really is just a different way for people to be thinking about what they're looking to make happen in the world.
zh: 而且我认为虽然客户有一些重叠，但这确实是人们思考自己想要在这个世界上实现什么的不同方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could, of course, you know, not to tempt anyone here, they could maybe, but I think it's a very, it would be very difficult and a very hard thing that would require different branding, you know, different setup, different product, all of that.
zh: 当然可以，你知道，不是在这里诱惑任何人，他们也许可以，但我认为这会是非常、会非常困难且非常艰难的事情，需要不同的品牌定位，你知道，不同的搭建、不同的产品，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and also you're at a scale now where the build by partner analysis for Airbnb would be very different than it was then.
zh: 嗯，而且你现在所处的规模，使得 Airbnb 的“自建还是合作”分析与当时会非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, scale is the ultimate moat for a marketplace, right?
zh: 是的，我的意思是，规模是市场平台的终极护城河，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like network effects are amazing and it's just, it's so fun to build a business that I couldn't imagine
zh: 比如网络效应太神奇了，而且打造一门这样的生意真是太有趣了，我无法想象

speaker: Unknown
en: Feeling this level of enthusiasm for the business we're building if I didn't understand and see every day how every unit of supply we add makes it better for every camper and every camper we add makes it better for every host.
zh: 如果我不理解、不能每天亲眼看到我们增加的每一单位供给让每一位露营者的体验更好、我们增加的每一位露营者让每一位房主的体验更好，我还会对我们在打造的这门生意抱有这种程度的热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that to me, that scale, that network effect is what, you know, that's what's so exciting about the business model.
zh: 对我来说，那种规模、那种网络效应，就是，你知道，这就是这个商业模式如此令人兴奋的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: When did you know it was working?
zh: 你是什么时候知道它行得通的？

speaker: Unknown
en: We partnered with a really large, I think it was like a regenerative organic farmers association.
zh: 我们与一个非常大的组织合作，我记得好像是某种再生有机农民协会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had them email their newsletter and say, hey, if you want to host camping, sign up.
zh: 我们让他们在他们的新闻通讯里发邮件说，嘿，如果你想举办露营，就来注册。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't know, do people want to do this?
zh: 我们不知道，人们想不想做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do people not want to do this?
zh: 人们是不是不想做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember waking up that morning where they'd sent out the newsletter that morning and opening up our backend systems.
zh: 我记得那天早上他们发出那封新闻通讯后，我醒来打开我们的后台系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we'd gotten like four or five people to sign up at that point.
zh: 我记得当时我们大概只招到了四五个注册的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there were hundreds.
zh: 而那里有好几百个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I got to just scroll through.
zh: 我就这样一条条往下翻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I started crying.
zh: 然后我开始哭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I bet.
zh: 我猜也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cause you're like, oh.
zh: 因为你就像，哦。

speaker: Unknown
en: People want this.
zh: 人们想要这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my inbox was full of notes from people who were like, we've been talking about doing this for years.
zh: 而且我的收件箱里塞满了人们的留言，他们都说，我们谈论做这件事已经好多年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got the perfect, I remember like a strawberry farm on an island.
zh: 我们有完美的——我记得是一个岛上的草莓农场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were like, well, we couldn't afford the insurance, but we couldn't figure out how to market it.
zh: 他们说，我们付不起保险，但我们也不知道该怎么营销。

speaker: Unknown
en: We couldn't figure out how to reach people.
zh: 我们没法想明白该怎么触达人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, oh, this is going to work.
zh: 然后我就想，哦，这事儿能成。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew we had demand.
zh: 我知道我们有需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's never been the problem.
zh: 这从来都不是问题所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we have supply.
zh: 现在我们有了供给。

speaker: Unknown
en: What an incredible signal.
zh: 多么了不起的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will you situate us where in the journey you are when this happens?
zh: 你能跟我们讲讲这件事发生时你们处在旅程的哪个阶段吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's probably 2017 or so.
zh: 那大概是 2017 年左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the biggest challenges you've had to tackle that you didn't foresee that night in your North Beach Italian restaurant?
zh: 在你 North Beach 的那家意大利餐厅的那个晚上，有哪些你没能预见的、后来不得不应对的最大挑战？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think helping people think through infrastructure and the right thing is important.
zh: 我觉得帮助人们想清楚基础设施、想清楚什么是对的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably regulations are another one.
zh: 法规大概是另一个挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you familiar with AB 518?
zh: 你熟悉 AB 518 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I am because I prepped for our conversation.
zh: 我熟悉，因为我为我们的对话做了准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just last year, California passed pretty amazing legislation that creates a new regulatory framework counties can opt into that allows people who have, you know, bigger parcels, mostly targeting farmers, ranchers, land trusts, things like that, to have up to nine campsites.
zh: 就在去年，加州通过了一项相当了不起的立法，创设了一个县可以选择加入的新监管框架，允许那些拥有较大地块的人——主要针对农民、牧场主、土地信托之类——拥有最多九个营地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Without needing to get the really onerous permit that is required for like an RV park before there wasn't like a separate lane for these lower impact type of campsites.
zh: 而不需要去办理像房车公园那样真正繁重的许可，以前并没有为这类低影响的营地单独开辟一条通道。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has totally changed the game.
zh: 这彻底改变了局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's been amazing to see the coalition around this, right?
zh: 所以看到围绕这件事的联盟真是很棒，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's everyone from, you know, the Farm Bureau to the Nature Conservancy.
zh: 从 Farm Bureau 到 Nature Conservancy，所有人都在其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when's the last time like all the farmers and all the conservationists and all the small rural businesses all agreed on something.
zh: 想想上一次所有农民、所有环保人士和所有乡村小企业在一件事上达成一致是什么时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Outdoor rec is such a powerful economic engine.
zh: 户外休闲是一个如此强大的经济引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like outdoor recreation means trails.
zh: 户外休闲意味着步道。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means boat ramps.
zh: 意味着船坡道。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not just going to bring in visitors.
zh: 那不只是会带来游客。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great for the people who live there as well.
zh: 对住在那里的人们也很有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's really created, I think, a groundswell of support around, you know, regulations to better support more, more outdoor recreation.
zh: 所以我认为这真正在法规周围营造出了一种支持更多户外休闲的支持浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's been the biggest challenge since you incorporated private land and HIP and HIP camp really took off?
zh: 那么自你把私有土地纳入、HIP camp 真正起飞以来，最大的挑战是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for me personally, the biggest challenge has been managing my own health and energy.
zh: 我觉得对我个人而言，最大的挑战一直是管理我自己的健康和精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, same work.
zh: 哦，同样的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is that?
zh: 为什么会这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a pretty obsessive person and very passionate, and I believe so much in what we're doing that it can get really easy, and especially maybe a few years ago, to start talking yourself into making sacrifices that don't make sense.
zh: 我是个相当执着的人，也非常有激情，我对我们正在做的事情深信不疑，以至于很容易——尤其是几年前——开始说服自己去做一些不合理的牺牲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sacrifice sleep.
zh: 牺牲睡眠。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sacrifice a workout.
zh: 牺牲锻炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sacrifice a healthy dinner, right?
zh: 牺牲一顿健康的晚餐，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like these kind of little things that each one on their own feels like justified in the moment, but over the course of a few years really starts to pile up.
zh: 就是这类小事，每一件单独看在当下都显得情有可原，但积累几年之后就真的开始堆积起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got shingles at one point.
zh: 我有一次得了带状疱疹。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel very lucky I went into the ER that day and the doctor took one look at me and said, this is shingles.
zh: 我觉得自己非常幸运，那天我去了急诊室，医生看了我一眼就说，这是带状疱疹。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're way too young for shingles.
zh: 你得带状疱疹实在太年轻了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we talk about our job?
zh: 我们能聊聊你的工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's going on?
zh: 怎么回事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they knew this was stressful.
zh: 因为他们知道这压力很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 的确如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 的确如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think learning to build the right systems, the right habits, there's no glory in becoming unhealthy in pursuit of this mission.
zh: 所以我觉得要学会建立正确的系统、正确的习惯，在追求这个使命的过程中搞垮身体是没有任何荣耀可言的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd say the real unlock is more knowing that your body and mind are worth taking care of.
zh: 所以我想说真正的突破更多是认识到你的身体和头脑值得被照顾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that if you're really in solving a problem and building a scaled organization that's gonna help shape culture for decades, you gotta take care of yourself and like you are worth taking care of.
zh: 而且如果你真的致力于解决一个问题、打造一个将帮助塑造未来几十年文化的规模化组织，你就得照顾好自己，你值得被照顾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, so many times I'll talk to early stage founders who are just really struggling and they're exhausted.
zh: 所以很多时候，我会和那些真的非常挣扎、筋疲力尽的早期创始人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, okay, let's try to take care of that first.
zh: 我会说，好吧，我们先把那个照顾好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the second you're tired, you lose your creativity, you lose your problem solving, you come up to a challenge and instead of getting curious about how to get around it, it feels like a, you know, a drama, stress, it's the end.
zh: 因为你一累，就失去了创造力，失去了解决问题的能力，你遇到一个挑战时，与其对如何绕过它充满好奇，它反而像是一场——你知道的——戏剧、压力，像是末日。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think, yeah, that's actually probably been the hardest, the hardest part of all of this for me.
zh: 所以我觉得，是的，这实际上可能是这一切中最难的部分，对我来说最难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big is the company now?
zh: 公司现在有多大？

speaker: Unknown
en: Close to 100.
zh: 接近 100 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're now the largest search engine for public land.
zh: 我们现在是最大的公共土地搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're the largest search engine and booking engine for commercial campgrounds, which we haven't gotten into yet.
zh: 我们是最大的商业露营地搜索引擎和预订引擎，这一点我们还没有深入讲过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of the benefits of scaling this company through private land is now all the existing campgrounds also can benefit.
zh: 但通过私有土地来扩展这家公司的好处之一是，现在所有现有的露营地也都能受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can join.
zh: 它们可以加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we're sending more bookings now to commercial campgrounds in the US than any other platform by nearly an order of magnitude.
zh: 而且我认为我们现在发给美国商业露营地的预订量比任何其他平台都多，差距接近一个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, we're the largest search and booking engine for private land, which is a category
zh: 然后，当然，我们是最大的私有土地搜索和预订引擎，这是一个品类——

speaker: Unknown
en: Um, we essentially created and have really been able to scale.
zh: 嗯，基本上是我们开创的，并且真正能够把它做大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's really those three pillars together that have, um, created the HipCamp of today.
zh: 所以正是这三根支柱加在一起，嗯，造就了今天的 HipCamp。

speaker: Unknown
en: Alissa, is the company remote, hybrid, or in-person?
zh: Alissa，公司是远程、混合还是线下办公？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're mostly work from home, but we do a lot of in-person work.
zh: 我们大部分时间在家办公，但我们做很多线下工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm happy to talk about that because that was a whole journey.
zh: 我很乐意谈谈这个，因为那是一段完整的历程。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you, how do you do in-person?
zh: 你怎么，你们怎么做线下工作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots of ways we do.
zh: 有很多方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a space in San Francisco we go to sometimes, but then we do a lot of like onsites where we bring everyone together.
zh: 我们在旧金山有一个空间，有时会去，然后我们会做很多类似 onsites 的活动，把大家聚在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone, but like the right group of people.
zh: 不是所有人，而是合适的那群人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm working with people in person probably like almost every week, every other week.
zh: 所以我大概几乎每周、每隔一周就会和人们线下一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we do bigger company camping trips and campouts.
zh: 然后我们还会组织更大的公司露营之旅和露营活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you do onsites at campsites?
zh: 所以你们在营地做 onsite？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes, yes.
zh: 有时是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what do those look like?
zh: 那些是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Generally, it's like we've identified a really important problem.
zh: 一般来说，就是我们发现了一个非常重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just certain problems I think are really hard to solve on Zoom.
zh: 我认为有些问题真的很难在 Zoom 上解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you feel that, you just like fly everybody in and you're like, we're solving this.
zh: 当你感觉到这一点时，你就把所有人都飞过来，然后说，我们要解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not leaving until we do.
zh: 解决之前我们不离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one thing to bring everyone into an office.
zh: 把所有人带进办公室是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's another thing to bring everyone to Mendocino Magic or another one of the campsites with which you work.
zh: 把所有人带到 Mendocino Magic 或者你们合作的另一个露营地是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: What drives you to bring people out into nature to one of your partners and set up on the land and work there?
zh: 是什么驱使你把人们带到大自然中，带到你们的一个合作伙伴那里，在土地上安顿下来并在那里工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for us being at a hip camp means you get to see the product in action and it's just deeply inspiring.
zh: 我认为对我们来说，在一家 hip camp 意味着你能看到产品实际运作，这非常鼓舞人心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's so much more meaningful if we're talking about how do we create more great campsites.
zh: 比如说，如果我们讨论的是如何创造更多优质的露营地，那意义就大得多——

speaker: Unknown
en: Our number one objective has been for a long time if we actually get to go walk the land.
zh: 长期以来我们的头号目标一直是，如果我们真的能去走一走那片土地。

speaker: Unknown
en: So recently we had an onsite out in Stinson.
zh: 所以最近我们在 Stinson 附近做了一次 onsite。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to go walk around Slide Ranch, which is a beautiful hip camp and nonprofit that has a mission to get more kids rooted in nature and they have great campsites and they use that revenue to fund scholarships.
zh: 我们去参观了 Slide Ranch，那是一个很美的 hip camp 和非营利组织，其使命是让更多孩子扎根于大自然，他们有很棒的露营地，并用那笔收入来资助奖学金。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to walk around, hear from the host about those scholarships, about the direct impact our work is having on helping her organization go from being in a pretty serious deficit.
zh: 我们得以四处走走，听房东讲那些奖学金，讲我们的工作对帮助她的组织从相当严重的赤字状态——

speaker: Unknown
en: To being in the black.
zh: ——转变为盈余状态所产生的直接影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we got to walk through the campsite and see the people who were like setting up their tents and we're gonna camp on the edge of the Pacific Ocean for the night and seeing people having these moments of exhale and peace and being like that's what all of our hard work is making possible when we talk about having
zh: 然后我们走过露营地，看到那些正在搭帐篷的人，他们要在太平洋边上露营一晚，看到人们拥有这种舒缓和平静的时刻，然后想说，这就是我们所有的努力工作所实现的东西，当我们谈到——

speaker: Unknown
en: Our core company, North Star, is nights outside.
zh: 我们公司的核心北极星是户外过夜数。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's our core KPI.
zh: 那是我们的核心 KPI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're always tracking and working towards.
zh: 我们一直在追踪并为之努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you get to the millions, it can start to feel abstract.
